description: Tuned for a solo maintainer. The failure mode being designed against is not stale
dependencies, it is thirty open PRs that nobody reads, after which the maintainer stops
reading all of them and the security ones go past unnoticed too.
So: routine updates are batched, quiet and automerged; anything that can actually break
the build waits for a human; and security fixes escape every one of those restrictions.
NOTE: GitHub's own Dependabot SECURITY ALERTS stay enabled separately in repository
settings. Renovate and Dependabot alerts are different products and there is no conflict:
Dependabot tells us a CVE exists, Renovate opens the PR that fixes it. Do not disable
Dependabot alerts just because Renovate is handling version bumps — only Dependabot's
VERSION UPDATE PRs (.github/dependabot.yml) should stay off, to avoid duplicate PRs.
Routine non-major updates: one grouped PR, automerged once CI is green. These are the
ones that generate volume and almost never need a decision.
Majors always wait for a human. Astro 6 -> 7, Zod 3 -> 4 and Wrangler 3 -> 4 were each
a day of work in this stack; none of them should arrive as an automerged PR at 3am.
They appear on the dependency dashboard as checkboxes and open a PR only when ticked.
The Cloudflare toolchain has to move together. @astrojs/cloudflare declares peer ranges
on both astro and wrangler, so bumping one alone produces an install that resolves but
does not deploy.
Zod is the contract boundary — every eCFR schema and the public API's OpenAPI document
derive from it. A minor that changes error shapes or inference is worth reading, and
@hono/zod-openapi pins a zod peer range, so they travel together.
fast-xml-parser parses 810 MB of upstream XML and its output shape decides what gets
counted. Never automerged: a parser behaviour change is a silent measurement change,
which is precisely the class of bug this codebase was rewritten to eliminate.
GitHub Actions: grouped and automerged for minor and patch. Majors still need approval
— action majors routinely change the runner's Node version or an input name.
Node and pnpm are pinned in three places (engines, packageManager, .nvmrc) and a bump
has to land in all of them at once. Always a human decision.
Security fixes bypass every restriction above: no 3-day soak, no Monday-morning window,
no grouping, no dashboard approval. A fix that waits for the batch is not a fix.
